newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent weaker, buyers relaxed arb closed.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent weaker, buyers relaxed arb closed.

text.p: North Sea physical and paper Brent prices edged lower on Wednesday with little sign of fresh buying interest and a closed transatlantic arbitrage weighing on the market, traders said.
"There are no buyers and even the (transatlantic arbitrage) is closed." one trader said, "At Least in the past we had the pretence of an arb, but there's nothing there this time."
A Feb 26-28 Brent traded at March Brent +5 cents -- down from a +12 cent deal on Tuesday for a Feb 22-24 loader.
The equity holders said the cargo was additional to the original programme. It was heard destined for Eastern Europe.
Few buyers were seen for the remaining three Feb cargoes and one seller asked March +5 -- down from an early offer at +15.
A clutch of early March Forties cargoes moved, all around the steady level of dated Brent +40 cents, but an early March cargo of Flotta traded 5-10 cents down at dated Brent -60 cents.
Brent equity holders expected the March loading programme, not expected to hold many surprises, to be released on Thursday.
"It'll just be up a bit because of the longer month," one equity holder said.
March/April paper eased around 3-4 cents on the day to around +32/34 cents with April/May at +28/31 cents.
Next week's Cfds were pegged around April Brent +24/27 cents March after talking March Brent -8/-5 cents in early business.
In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals was discussed steady to around five cents easier at dated Brent -85 cents a barrel cif Genoa, traders said.
They said see-saw action on Brent futures discouraged activity and the impact of loading delays at the Black Sea port of Novorossiisk balanced slack spot demand from refiners, traders said.
"Everything is about the same level (compared to Wednesday morning). Things looks just about balanced," a trader said.
